issue_context.title: Creating a WebWorker inside a WebWorker will the self.origin value being null.
issue_context.body:
### Describe the bug

When the origin value is null, calling some APIs can trigger SecurityError or Cross-Origin error.

For example, executing await navigator.storage.getDirectory()
will throw the error: Error: SecurityError: Storage directory access is denied.

The reason is that a WebWorker was created using a Data URL.
![image](https://github.com/vitejs/vite/assets/3307051/7289aee6-91dc-447d-8d24-d27c910095ca)

The corresponding Vite code is at: https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/7b240e408ed83f172e9f88823eae3b4a9ba92674/packages/vite/src/node/plugins/worker.ts#L326C28-L326C38

I tried replacing self with window, which resolved the issue.



### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-hfhdfg?file=main.js

### Steps to reproduce

1. `npm run build`
2. check `dist/assets/index-[hash].js`

### System Info

```shell
N/A
```


### Used Package Manager

npm

review_comments: If this old code was executed in a Worker (i.e., when it is a nested worker), it will error because `window` does not exist and fall back to loading by data URI. Is that what was happening in your case? I want to clarify it because IIUC this won't happen in non-nested worker.

Yes, the non-nested worker works fine. In a nested worker, the value of self.origin is 'null', which causes many APIs to be unusable due to the browser's same-origin policy.

Here is a simple code snippet to reproduce the error. Please try executing it in devtools.
```js
new Worker(
  "data:text/javascript;base64," + btoa(`
    console.log(111, self.origin === 'null')
    // test OPFS API
    navigator.storage.getDirectory() // => DOMException: Storage directory access is denied.
  `),
)
```
